seoTitle: Free Online Grep for Pasted Text with Context Lines
metaDescription: Filter pasted text with a plain or regex pattern like grep. Invert, whole word, line numbers, context before and after, count or matches only. Free.
intro: Runs a grep-style search on text you paste, with context lines, invert, whole-word matching and a count.
why:
Sometimes you only need to find the interesting lines in a log or export without opening a terminal. This tool offers the grep options people use most: -n line numbers, -v invert, -i ignore case, -w whole word, -A and -B context, -c count and -o matching parts only.

The output format follows GNU grep, so match lines use a colon and context lines use a dash, with -- between groups. The pattern is a JavaScript regular expression, which differs a little from POSIX or PCRE, for example in how \b and character classes work.
howTo: Enter a pattern and tick regex if it is an expression.
Choose options such as invert, whole word or context lines.

faq.q: Is this the same as GNU grep?
faq.a: The output layout and options match. The pattern syntax is JavaScript regex, not POSIX basic or extended expressions.

faq.q: How is the plain pattern treated?
faq.a: Special characters are escaped, so a dot means a dot and not any character.

faq.q: What does only the matching parts do?
faq.a: It prints each match on its own line, like grep -o. It cannot be combined with invert.
No. Everything runs in your browser.
